answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to post a refundable stake, then randomly select a small set of established agents as witnesses for its first transactions. The witnesses verify that the newcomer controls the claimed resources and have part of their own stake slashed if they attest to fraud. A public beacon announces each verification pulse, while the inlet accepts only identities with a completed check. A sybil attacker must therefore lock capital in every fake and risk losing it through colluding attestations, making mass identities costly rather than free.
